data.name: Gangesh
data.long_meaning: The name Gangesh is derived from the ancient Sanskrit language, and it refers to the god of the sacred and mighty Ganges River. This river is considered to be the most sacred and pure in Hinduism. The god Ganesha, also known as Ganapati, is the god of wisdom, knowledge, and new beginnings. He is often depicted as having an elephant head and multiple arms, and he is known to remove obstacles and bring good fortune.

data.cultural_impact: Gangesh's name carries a deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is associated with the revered and holy Ganges River. In Hindu mythology, the Ganges River is believed to have descended from heaven to earth out of compassion for the people. The river is considered to be a source of purification and is believed to wash away sins and impurities. The name Gangesh is a reminder of this powerful and transformative body of water, and it evokes a sense of respect and reverence for the cultural heritage and beliefs surrounding the Ganges River.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Gangesh is deeply significant as it represents the god Ganesha, who is revered as the remover of obstacles and the god of wisdom and knowledge. In Hindu mythology, Ganesha is worshipped before starting any new venture or undertaking a new project as he is believed to bless us with his wisdom and guide us towards success. The name Gangesh, therefore, carries the blessings and protection of this powerful and benevolent deity, and it infuses a sense of hope and inspiration in those who bear the name. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge, wisdom, and wisdom in all aspects of life, and of the transformative power of grace, compassion, and purification.
